Hi Natasha / Irene,

Following up with the technical pieces. Attached: redwood_subprocessors_20280602.csv and TIA_sample_redwood.docx. High-level notes:

- Subprocessor CSV includes: role, primary location (country), purpose, data types processed, and whether the processor is dual-residency (EU/US). We flag any that route via non-EU hops.
- SCCs: our legal mapping doc (short note included in the TIA sample) shows how SCCs are implemented for hosted API customers. For UK-specific flow, the UK IDTA addendum is our standard approach — we do not rely on separate bespoke agreements unless requested.
- Onshore fallback: technically feasible as an operational control (we can route EU-origin requests to EU pools and fall back to US pools with a configurable failover). Committing to strict contractual "EU-only" processing for all requests is operationally challenging for burst/burst overflow scenarios; we recommend an SLO + documented fallback clause (we can offer routing priority and a higher-tier Dedicated capacity option).
- Impact to telemetry/latency: routing to EU-only pools will increase tail latency for cold-starts if a request's KV cache isn't warm. TIA sample spells this out and suggests mitigation (warm pools, prefix caching).

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20280602.csv (attachment), TIA_sample_redwood.docx (attachment)

Happy to walk through the CSV if you want a short demo.

—Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
